_README: THE CONSTITUENT LIST. One line per company: the sleeve it belongs to, and
whether it is in or out.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A RULE. Two automated screens were built and both
selected the wrong universe:
BALANCE SHEET (crypto assets / total assets). Measures what proportion of a
company IS a pile of coins. Coinbase scored 5.5% and was excluded as
immaterial; Circle scored 0.14%. Greenlane Holdings, a $2m shell, scored 79%
and was a constituent. The test selects crypto HOLDINGS, not crypto
COMPANIES.
TEXT MATCHES (how many crypto phrases a 10-K contains). Coinbase matched 4.
Greenlane matched 5. A shell that pivoted writes expansively about its new
strategy while Coinbase describes its operations in plain, narrow language.
The signal runs backwards and no threshold on it separates them.
SEGMENT REVENUE would be the right measure and is not obtainable: it has no
standard XBRL element, companyfacts flattens the dimensions that carry it,
and most filers report no crypto segment at all.
So: judgment, recorded. Section 5 asks for a documented inclusion rule, and
'a named person judged each company against stated criteria, and every
decision is listed with its reason' is documented. What it is not is
automatic, and no published crypto-equity index is.
THE CRITERION APPLIED HERE: would this company's revenue or balance sheet be
materially different if crypto ceased to exist? Yes puts it in. A company
that merely accepts crypto, or mentions it in risk factors, is out.
CONFIDENCE MARKS. 'verify' means I am not certain of the ticker or the
current status and it should be checked before the index is published. This
list was assembled partly from a knowledge cutoff of May 2026 and partly from
search; several of these companies listed or renamed recently.

excluded._note: companies the automated screens admitted, excluded here with the reason
excluded.GNLN: Greenlane Holdings - $2m market capitalisation and a majority-crypto balance sheet only because the balance sheet is nearly empty. Not a crypto company by any reading of the business
excluded.IPST: IP Strategy Holdings - was Heritage Distilling; $2.5m
excluded.SCLX: Scilex Holding - a pharmaceutical company; the text screen called it a miner
excluded.DJT: Trump Media - a media company holding bitcoin. Arguable, and excluded because the business would be substantially unchanged without crypto
excluded._all_funds: every trust, ETF and ETP. §19: they hold crypto for their shareholders, which is custody and not issuer treasury, and including them counts the same coins twice
excluded.IREN: holds ZERO bitcoin and is projected at ~71% of revenue from AI and HPC by end 2026, with a Microsoft contract and an Nvidia partnership. It is an AI cloud provider with a mining history. By the stated criterion - would revenue or the balance sheet be materially different if crypto ceased to exist - the answer is no
excluded.WULF: exiting bitcoin mining ENTIRELY by 2026. HPC lease revenue from Anthropic and Fluidstack reached 71% of total while mining revenue fell to $12.8m. Same criterion, same answer

open_questions: AI AND HPC. Riot leases data-centre capacity to AI tenants under a twenty-year agreement; Galaxy is building AI data centres; Core Scientific, IREN and TeraWulf all have material HPC exposure. §8 requires those economics separated where identifiable. They are NOT separated here, so the mining sleeve currently contains a large and growing quantity of AI infrastructure. This is the single largest unresolved issue in the classification.
MINED INVENTORY VERSUS TREASURY. §19 for every miner that also holds. Not decided.
ENCUMBRANCE. CleanSpark posts 29% of its holdings as derivative collateral. Whether the index measures gross or unencumbered holdings applies to every miner posting collateral.
HOOD SHARE COUNT. Robinhood stopped tagging shares outstanding in February 2022. Until a count is supplied it cannot be weighted, and it is one of the largest constituents by value.

ai_rule.rule: a company leaves the index when crypto stops being material to it, judged by the same criterion used to admit it
ai_rule.why: The miners are not what they were. IREN, TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher and Hut 8 have all moved capacity to AI and high-performance computing, and the sector beat bitcoin by 70% in 2026 BECAUSE of that pivot rather than because of crypto. An index that keeps them all is partly measuring the AI trade wearing a mining ticker.

retained_with_material_ai.CORZ: aggressive pivot, still mining. Re-check when HPC passes half of revenue
retained_with_material_ai.HUT: data centres alongside mining and a treasury
retained_with_material_ai.RIOT: a twenty-year Rockdale lease but no major AI revenue yet; still primarily a miner

ai_rule.the_judgment_that_remains: Where a company is halfway through the pivot there is no clean line, and the boundary moves as they execute. This should be reviewed each quarter, and the review is a judgment rather than a threshold - segment revenue would settle it and is not obtainable from XBRL.
